Scene-embedded geometric computations. Foundation gallery — spatial algorithms demonstrated through environment geometry.
Medial axis as skeleton: the locus of inscribed circles that captures a shape's topological essence. Thinning geometry to its structural core.
Signed distance fields: every point in space knows how far it is from the nearest surface. The implicit representation that powers modern rendering and collision.
Dilation, erosion, opening, closing: structuring elements sweep across shapes, adding or removing boundary pixels. Image processing as geometric sculpting.
Divide and conquer finds the nearest two points in O(n log n). Fibonacci sequences provide spatial distribution context for the geometric search.
Sweep line algorithm: a vertical line scans left to right, detecting segment crossings. Event-driven geometry turning O(n²) brute force into elegance.
Ray casting: shoot a ray from the point, count boundary crossings. Odd means inside, even means outside. The simplest topological test in computational geometry.
Gift wrapping, Graham scan, quickhull: multiple strategies for finding the tightest convex boundary. The rubber band around the nails — minimal enclosure as geometric synthesis.
Every pixel labeled with its distance to the nearest feature: the distance transform that enables Voronoi computation, path planning, and morphological analysis.
